story.sq02.title: Hours for the River
story.sq02.summary: Agree on a specific lower-valley water schedule through dated courier letters. A confirmed allocation agreement is one requirement for Returning Rain.
story.sq02.s1.objective: Read the mill and reed-village requests and compare their minimum water needs.
story.sq02.s1.journal: Mill Keeper Su needs four hours of steady flow for grain. Weaver He needs two hours to rinse reed fiber. Both reserve drinking water first. Two schedules fit those needs; I must send one and wait for an actual reply.
story.sq02.s1.lan: I used to write “give the valley enough.” Enough for whom, and at what hour? These two finally put numbers beside their names.
story.sq02.s1.apprentice: We can promise hours and a low-flow stop rule. We cannot promise water the mountain does not have.
story.sq02.s1.note: Requests received this morning. Su: “Four hours daily will clear the grain queue. Twice a week we can mill at dusk if the sluice is lit.” He: “Two rinse hours; dawn or afternoon both work. Do not trade away the household drinking reserve. Our signed reply must precede any gate change.”
story.sq02.s2.objective: Choose and dispatch a written schedule with a drinking reserve and shortage rule.
story.sq02.s2.journal: Schedule A: mill 06:00–10:00; reed rinse 14:00–16:00. Schedule B: rinse 06:00–08:00; mill 08:00–12:00, shifting to 16:00–20:00 on market days, days two and five of each seven-day cycle. Day one is the posting day. Both keep the marked household drinking reserve. No reply has arrived yet.
story.sq02.s2.lan: The first plan spreads demand. The second frees the afternoon for repairs, but gives the mill two evening shifts. They offered those shifts themselves. Write the tradeoff plainly.
story.sq02.s2.clue: Both proposals: reserve the cistern’s blue drinking-water mark before work releases; stop milling and rinsing when the gauge drops below the red work mark; post a same-day notice; review in seven days. The courier round trip takes eighteen in-game hours.
story.sq02.s2.choice_a: Send Schedule A: morning milling, afternoon rinsing.
story.sq02.s2.choice_b: Send Schedule B: dawn rinsing, rotating mill shifts.
story.sq02.s2.reply_a: The proposal is sealed. Its travel time begins now; I will check the returned signatures before approving a gate change.
story.sq02.s2.reply_b: The evening shifts and their lamp check are written into the proposal. I will wait for both signatures.
story.sq02.s3.objective: Read both returned signatures, then confirm and post the agreed schedule.
story.sq02.s3.journal: Returning Rain requirement: allocation agreed. Dispatch alone does not qualify. I need both dated replies and a posted schedule. I can revise an accepted schedule later by repeating the courier exchange.
story.sq02.s3.lan: The courier has returned after eighteen hours. Two signatures, the same reserve line, the same review date. Read them before you hang the board.
story.sq02.s3.apprentice: The signatories accepted this schedule, including its shortage rule. I will post the actual hours, not just the word “agreed.”
story.sq02.s3.record: Returned agreement, dispatched eighteen hours before delivery: “Su, Mill Keeper, and He, Reed Weaver, accept the enclosed selected schedule without amendments. Drinking reserve first; both workshops stop below the red mark. Su and He check the gauge before their own work slots; physical gauge upkeep is covered by the separate maintenance charter. First review: seven days after posting. If supply falls, renegotiate hours before lowering the drinking reserve.”
story.sq02.s3.confirm: Verify both signatures and post the selected schedule.
story.sq02.s3.retry: Replies have not arrived. Rest at the sanctuary to receive them, or continue another task. The proposal is preserved and has not taken effect.
story.sq02.s3.done: Allocation agreement confirmed. Its schedule, reserve, stop rule, and review date are visible on the board.
story.sq02.epilogue.open: Seven days after reopening, Su and He review the selected schedule. They keep the drinking reserve and adjust work hours around the apprentice’s seasonal regulation. Their first disagreement is recorded instead of concealed.
story.sq02.epilogue.seal: The allocation board moves to Yun’s prepared alternative channel. The same households retain the drinking reserve; milling hours shrink during the move and are renegotiated at the scheduled review.
story.sq02.epilogue.shared: Seven days into the shared cycle, the signatories check the gauge together. They change two work hours after a dry spell without treating a signed agreement as an endless claim on the river.
story.sq02.pending_status: Accepted plan: {effective}. Proposal awaiting confirmation: {pending}. The final decision uses the accepted plan, not an unanswered proposal.
